intended_object: The unit-slope presentation (start index, initial height, length, nondecreasing edge slopes) of a convex real height sequence h : ℕ → ℝ ∪ {∞} whose finite domain is the interval [l, l+k], i.e. the inverse of the cumulative-sum map `FiniteSlopeData.heights` (from the docstring, the module doc and the round-trip lemmas).
explanation: The definition sets start := l, length := k, initialHeight := (h l).untop₀ and slope i := unitSlope h (l+i) = h(l+i+1) − h(l+i). `initialHeight` is the real height h l, which is finite by hdom. Each slope is a genuine edge slope, since both endpoints lie in [l, l+k] when i < k. Monotonicity follows from the convexity field `IsConvexSeq.monotoneOn` on finite edges. The degenerate case k = 0 gives the one-point polygon with no slopes. The empty polygon is excluded because hdom forces h l ≠ ⊤. The library proves both round trips (`heights_ofIsConvexSeq` and `ofIsConvexSeq_heights`), which confirms it is exactly the slope presentation of h. The restriction to ℝ is inherited from the library's `IsConvexSeq`, `unitSlope` and `finiteEdges`, which are all defined for ℕ → WithTop ℝ. This extraction is the converse of the real-valued `isConvexSeq_heights`, so its setting is dictated by the notion it consumes. Mathlib has no notion of convex WithTop-valued sequences or slope presentations, so there is no counterpart.
